inline.s: When false twofold discrimination arises, dharmas are in truth beyond existence and nonexistence.
Beyond the four propositions, from the two views apart;
The twofold born of discrimination, once known, is born no more.
In what is unborn one knows birth, in birth one knows the unborn;
Because those dharmas are equal, one should not give rise to discrimination.”
“May the Buddha tell me the principle that refutes the two views;
So that I and the rest of the assembly may never fall into existence or nonexistence.”
“Not mingled with the sectarians, and beyond the two vehicles;
What the Buddhas have realized and practiced is where the Buddha's sons do not fall back.
Liberation is neither cause nor non-cause, one and the same unborn mark;
Deluded, one clings to different names; the wise should always keep far from them.
Dharmas are born of discrimination, like a hair-wheel, an illusion, a mirage;
The sectarians vainly discriminate that the world arises from a self-nature.
The unborn, suchness, emptiness of nature, and true reality;
These are taught as different names; one should not cling to them as nonexistence.
As a hand has many names, so too does Indra have many names;
So too are all dharmas; one should not cling to them as nonexistence.
Form is not different from emptiness, and the unborn is the same;
One should not cling to them as different: that brings the fault of every view.
By discriminating the general and the particular, and by all-pervading discrimination;
One clings to the marks of all things, long and short, square and round.
Discriminating the general is mind, all-pervading discrimination is manas;
Discriminating the particular is consciousness, all beyond the marks of grasped and grasper.
To give rise to views within my Dharma, and the non-arising of the sectarians;
Both are false discrimination, their faults equal and no different.
If one can understand the non-arising that I have taught;
And what non-arising is for, that person understands my Dharma.
To break every view, non-arising dharmas have no dwelling place;
That these two meanings may be known, I teach the Dharma of non-arising.
If the non-arising I teach were existence or nonexistence;
It would be one with the sectarians' doctrine of non-arising without cause.
What I teach is the measure of Mind-only, far removed from existence and nonexistence;
Whether it be birth or no birth, such views should all be abandoned.
The doctrine of no cause does not arise; where there is birth, one clings to a maker;
With a maker, views are mixed; without one, things arise of themselves.”
“The Buddha teaches all skillful means, right view, the great vows, and the like;
If all dharmas were nonexistent, how could the seat of enlightenment be won?”
“Free from the grasped and the grasper, neither born nor ceasing;
The dharmas and non-dharmas one sees all arise from one's own mind.”
“What the Sage has spoken is at odds with itself;
How can he teach all dharmas and then speak of non-arising?
Living beings cannot understand; may the Buddha explain it for me;
That we may leave the sectarians' fault and their cause of inversion.
May the Supreme Teacher proclaim both birth and cessation;
All free from existence and nonexistence, yet without destroying cause and effect.”
“The world falls into the two extremes, deluded by all its views;
May the Blue-Lotus-Eyed One teach the stages of the grounds in order.
Grasping at birth and no birth, one does not know the cause of quiescence;
At the seat of enlightenment nothing is gained, and I too have nothing to teach.
Momentary dharmas are all empty, unborn and without self-nature;
The Buddhas have purified duality; to hold two is itself a fault.”
“Covered by wrong views, one discriminates—that is not the Tathāgata;
Vainly reckoning birth and cessation, may he explain it for us.”
“Accumulated through idle talk, born of concordant conditions;
Each appears before its kind, and form-objects are all complete.
Having seen outer forms, one gives rise to discrimination;
If one can understand this, then one sees the true meaning.
If the great elements were absent, no thing could be produced;
The great elements being Mind-only, know that nothing is born.
This mind too is unborn; then one accords with the noble lineage;
Do not discriminate discrimination; non-discrimination is wisdom.
To discriminate discrimination is duality, not nirvāṇa;
To posit a thesis of non-arising destroys the dharmas of illusion.
And without a cause illusion cannot arise, so one's own thesis is diminished;
Like an image in a mirror, which is free from the one and the different.
What is seen is not nonexistent, and the mark of birth is likewise;
Like a city of the gandharvas or an illusion, all await causes and conditions to exist.
So too are all dharmas: this is birth, not non-arising;
One discriminates a person and dharmas, and so gives rise to two kinds of self.
This is but worldly talk, and the foolish do not know it;
By vows and gathered conditions, by self-power and by the Supreme;
The fifth is the doctrine of the hearers, and there are arhats and the like;
Time, interval, and destruction, ultimate meaning and succession.
These four kinds of impermanence the foolish discriminate, and they are not wisdom;
The foolish fall into the two extremes: the qualities, the atoms, a self-nature as maker.
Clinging to the doctrines of existence and nonexistence, they do not know the cause of liberation;
The great elements oppose each other—how could they give rise to form?
They are only the nature of the great elements; there is no form made of them;
Fire burns up form, and water rots and destroys it.
Wind scatters and annihilates it—how then can form be born?
Form-aggregate and consciousness-aggregate: only these two, and not the five.
The rest are but other names; I speak of them as foes;
The differences of mind and mental factors give rise to manifest dharmas.
Analyzing all forms, Mind-only makes nothing;
Blue and white await each other, and so do maker and made.
The produced and emptiness of nature, cold and heat, the characterized and the mark;
Existence, nonexistence, and all the rest are vain reckonings that do not hold.
Mind, manas, and the other six—the consciousnesses all work together;
All arise from the storehouse consciousness, neither one nor different.
The Sāṃkhyas, the Vaiśeṣikas, and the naked ascetics reckon Ishvara as the producer;
All fall into the doctrines of existence and nonexistence, far from the meaning of quiescence.
The great elements produce form and mark, and are not born from the great elements;
The sectarians say the great elements give birth to the great elements and to form.
Outside the Dharma of non-arising, the sectarians reckon a maker;
Relying on the doctrines of existence and nonexistence, the foolish do not know.
The pure and true mark is yet joined with great wisdom;
It accords with mind alone, and is not the concord of manas and the rest.
If all karma gave birth to form, it would contradict the cause of the aggregates;
Living beings should then have no grasping, and none would dwell in the formless.
To say that form is nonexistent means living beings too should not exist;
The doctrine of the formless is annihilation, and the consciousnesses should not arise.
Consciousness dwells relying on four supports—how could the formless be achieved?
Since inner and outer are both unachieved, consciousness too should not arise.
If the consciousness of living beings were absent, they would naturally win liberation;
This must be a sectarian doctrine, and those who vainly reckon do not know it.
Some, following their liking, cling to the aggregates of the intermediate state;
As when one is born in the formless, how can the formless exist?
The form within the formless is not something that can be seen;
The formless then contradicts one's thesis, and there is no vehicle or rider.
Consciousness is born from habitual tendencies, and joins with the faculties;
The eight kinds, in a single instant, are all ungraspable.
